result.notes: 1) Reconciled test/specs/REQ-155.md (written pre-implementation) against the actual executor_test.exs: rewrote it end-to-end to describe the real T1-T8 tests by their actual test names/assertions, and added an explicit 'Deviation from the original T2 design' section documenting why the pcall-then-second-loop script was replaced with the pcall-then-goto-loop script (this runtime's :max_instructions counter is permanently exhausted once tripped, so a second while/for loop would be terminated by layer 1 alone and would not prove layer 2's necessity; a goto loop is not instrumented by the budget counter at all, confirmed empirically by ELIXIR-DEV and independently verified by SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER reading the vendored tv-labs/lua runtime source). 2) Mapped all 8 real acceptance_criteria from docs/requirements.yaml (not paraphrased) to specific tests -- see ac_to_test_mapping. Found and closed 2 real coverage gaps in T7 (AC-6) and T8 (AC-7): both original assertions were satisfiable by substrings that did not actually pin the claim requirement's own text tied to the right subject/clause -- added targeted assertions to executor_test.exs for both, then re-ran the suite. 3) Timing-margin re-check (fresh eyes): T1 uses timeout_ms 100 vs 600 with a 400ms upper bound on the short call (4x margin over the 100ms configured value) -- generous enough to absorb CI scheduling jitter without weakening the assertion that elapsed time tracks the configured value, not a hardcoded constant. T2/T4 use timeout_ms 300/100 with no additional wall-clock assertion beyond the returned tuple (no jitter risk). T3 uses timeout_ms 150 plus a fixed 50ms settle sleep before the before/after Task.Supervisor.children/1 comparison -- Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor is used by no other test file (grep-confirmed) and ExUnit runs tests within one Case module sequentially by default, so this snapshot comparison is not exposed to cross-test or cross-module interference; margin judged adequate. T6 uses timeout_ms 300 with a 50ms settle sleep before checking Task.Supervisor.children/1 is non-empty -- adequate margin, no upper-bound assertion that could flake under a slow CI host. No test asserts a tight upper bound on total test-file runtime. 4) No unseeded randomness anywhere in the REQ-155 describe block (no :rand, Enum.random, or similar) -- confirmed by inspection. 5) Test isolation under async: true confirmed: all REQ-155 tests use the /3-arity execute_with_manifest overload specifically to avoid any Application.put_env config swap; no test in the block mutates any shared global state (Application env, ETS, ...); the one piece of shared state read (Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor) is read-only via Task.Supervisor.children/1 and is confirmed used by no other test file, and within-module ExUnit execution is sequential by default, so no ordering hazard exists between T3/T6 and the rest of the suite. Real mix test output after all edits: `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 1.8 seconds (1.8s async, 0.00s sync)' / 'Result: 24 passed' / 0 failures, seed 300815.
